critique: The orange/yellow palette and rapid burst timing read as a fire effect, but it does not yet resemble an explosive muzzle flash. At 0.01s it is a soft, rounded orange blob with no sharp flame rays or directional blast silhouette. By 0.08s it has collapsed into a small, dense spark cluster rather than a sustained, expanding flash; the motion reads as a continuously replenished particle fountain instead of a brief explosive plume.

suggestions.why: Increase main-particle life so the burst remains visibly expanded at 0.08s and develops a readable flame/spark trail rather than disappearing into a tight cluster.
Widen directional spread to create the explosive fan/ray silhouette expected from a muzzle flash instead of the current compact rounded puff.
Make the initial hot particles larger so the flash has a stronger bright flame core before it breaks into smaller sparks.
